body:
This PR adds the `@params` macro, which can move any parameter struct from register memory to instruction memory. From a user perspective, this macro is equivalent to `@kwdef`, so any code that constructs, accesses, or dispatches off of parameter types can remain unchanged.

The macro's mode is set by the `CLIMA_PARAMS_MODE` preference (see [Preferences.jl](https://github.com/JuliaPackaging/Preferences.jl)), which is "type" by default and can be set to "bits" to switch back to the old `@kwdef` behavior. The "type" mode is the default because it lowers latency as well as register usage for code that uses one set of parameter values, which are constant-folded during compilation:
- CloudMicrophysics: all test files other than its two calibration tests compile and run 17.5% faster in total (e.g., the performance tests take 45% less time).
- ClimaAtmos: the flagship AMIP benchmark compiles 4.3% faster and runs 1.3% faster on an A100, and no kernel uses more registers.

The "bits" mode is meant for workflows that construct many parameter sets, like calibrations and large ensembles over parameters, where each new set would otherwise be a new type that has to be compiled (the two CloudMicrophysics calibration tests take 2.4 to 2.8 times longer in "type" mode).

Per struct, `@params` takes about 1.4 times as long as `@kwdef` to expand and evaluate (measured on the 74 parameter structs of CloudMicrophysics), plus about 0.2 s to compile the macro the first time it is used in a session.
